title: Hardware benchmark signatures and stability metrics for model serving variants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Define canonical benchmark 'signatures' and a stability scoring system for publishing hardware-specific performance profiles for model variants on A100, H100, L40S, and MI300. Deliverables: 1) signature JSON template used by automated onboarding runs, 2) stability score algorithm and thresholds for 'publishable' profiles, 3) documented pinning recommendations per hardware class (latency vs throughput trade-offs), 4) CI job configs and a sample published entry in the model catalog. Motivation: onboarding runs currently emit heterogeneous artifacts (CSV, logs, ad-hoc metrics) that make it hard for Console, routing, and billing to pick canonical per-hardware profiles. We need a repeatable, compact signature + score that runtime and Console can consume to make routing/pinning/fallback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A signature JSON schema (versioned) that includes: model_version, hw_family (A100/H100/L40S/MI300), sequence_length_distribution, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, median_tokens_per_request, tokens_per_sec, cost_estimate_per_1M_tokens, kv_cache_hit_percent, batch_size_optimal, quantization_mode, build_hash, run_timestamp
Stability score defined (0-100) computed from run-to-run variance of p95/p99, OOM rate, and quantization sensitivity; threshold >= 80 required to mark profile as publishable
Automated CI job (onboarding-smoke) produces signature and stability score and uploads to staging catalog for review
Documentation describing pin recommendations per hardware family and an example of fallback mapping (e.g., H100 -> A100 compatible variant) in Confluence
Integration test in runtime that reads signature and enforces pin gating logic in canary rollout scenario
One sample model variant (gpt-small-v2-quant) published to staging catalog with signatures for A100/H100/MI300/L40S
steps: 1) Draft signature JSON schema and internal field definitions
2) Implement ingestion helpers in onboarding pipeline to emit canonical signature
3) Run calibration matrix for sample models across hw classes (seq lengths 32/128/512) and collect metrics
4) Iterate on stability scoring formula with research (weight p99 variance higher than p95)
5) Add publish gating: only push profile to catalog if stability >= threshold and no OOMs observed
6) Add integration hooks in Console to display signature fields and deprecate old CSV artifacts
7) Create PRs: runtime hook + onboarding pipeline + catalog UI + docs
8) Run end-to-end canary: onboard model -> compute signatures -> publish to staging -> runtime canary routes -> validate SLA impact
notes: Trade-offs: a conservative stability threshold reduces false positives but slows publishing for newer hardware; we should add a 'trial' flag for profiles from experimental SKUs.
Quantization: 4-bit vs 8-bit behavior differs widely across MI300 vs A100; signatures must include quantization_mode to avoid bad fallbacks.
Cost estimate is an approximate guidance for customers and billing; compute it from tokens_per_sec and precomputed GPU cost/hour SKU table (stored in infra repo).
Backwards compatibility: the signature schema must be versioned so older Console/runtime can ignore unknown fields.
Edge case: sequence-length distributions with heavy tails (chat logs) should surface 'tail_fraction' so runtime can avoid batching that violates latency SLOs.
